basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 4.' and it opens 'Vers. 4. Circumcidit octava die. Circumcisio, cum ob multas figuras praecepta sit,'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 4. Circumcidit octava die. Circumcisio, cum ob multas figuras praecepta sit, specialiter figuram | Christi praetendit qui nos et in praesenti per baptismum vetere homine exuit, et in futuro per resurrectionem circumcidit in nobis omnem mortalitatem et corruptionem. Nam et quod in octava die circumcisus est Isaac designabatur octava saeculi aetas, quando generaliter resurrectio mortuorum celebrabitur.
